purpose: Machine-readable mapping between the Kafka-consumer serving path (processing-service -> tenant_metrics_daily, the source analytics-service and the dbt mart both read) and the dbt analytics-engineering path (dbt/models/marts/fct_tenant_daily_metrics.sql), documenting exactly which metrics are independently re-derived by two separate code paths versus which are a single source of truth simply re-exposed through dbt.
note_on_architecture: Only payment success and failure counts have independent derivations across the processing and dbt paths. dbt reads net_revenue, gross_revenue, order_count, units_sold, new_users, active_users, and churn_signal_count directly from tenant_metrics_daily, so those fields are passthrough and marked NOT_APPLICABLE for this comparison. dbt derives observed_successful_payments and observed_failed_payments by counting processed_payments, while the processing service incrementally updates payment_success_count and payment_failure_count. This contract compares those independently derived pairs.

reconciled_metrics.dbt_source: analytics_mart.fct_tenant_daily_metrics.observed_successful_payments (freshly COUNTed from processed_payments via dbt/models/staging/stg_payments.sql, status in authorized/captured)
reconciled_metrics.formula_serving: incremental counter, +1 per processed payment event with status in (authorized, captured)
reconciled_metrics.formula_dbt: count(*) filter (where status in ('captured', 'authorized')) from stg_payments grouped by tenant_id, metric_date
reconciled_metrics.source_of_truth_designation: Neither is authoritative by default -- an exact match is expected because both derive from the same processed_payments events; any divergence indicates a runtime defect (a missed/duplicated Kafka event, an off-by-one in the incremental upsert, or a stg_payments filter mismatch) and must be investigated, not silently trusted from one side.

reconciled_metrics.dbt_source: analytics_mart.fct_tenant_daily_metrics.observed_failed_payments (freshly COUNTed from processed_payments via stg_payments, status = failed)
reconciled_metrics.formula_serving: incremental counter, +1 per processed payment event with status = failed
reconciled_metrics.formula_dbt: count(*) filter (where status = 'failed') from stg_payments grouped by tenant_id, metric_date
reconciled_metrics.source_of_truth_designation: Same as payment_success_count -- exact match expected, divergence is a real defect signal.

passthrough_not_reconciled.reason: dbt's fct_tenant_daily_metrics reads this field directly from tenant_metrics_daily (select * from {{ source('platform', 'tenant_metrics_daily') }}) with no independent recomputation from processed_orders. There is only one code path today.
same as net_revenue -- passthrough from tenant_metrics_daily, no independent user-session recomputation in dbt today

dbt computes this as churn_signal_count / nullif(active_users, 0) using the same passthrough churn_signal_count and active_users fields above -- a derived ratio of single-source inputs, not an independent second measurement.

dbt computes this ratio from the Kafka-consumer's own payment_success_count/payment_failure_count (tenant_metrics_daily), not from the independently-observed stg_payments counts -- it is a derived ratio of the serving-path's own numbers. The underlying counts it derives from (payment_success_count, payment_failure_count) ARE reconciled above; the ratio itself is not separately reconciled because it adds no new information once the counts match.
passthrough_not_reconciled.status: NOT_APPLICABLE (covered indirectly via the underlying counts)

quality_gate.rule: critical mismatch (any reconciled_metrics row where abs(serving_value - dbt_value) > allowed_tolerance) -> reconciliation FAIL
quality_gate.behavior_on_fail: scripts/reconcile_kafka_dbt_metrics.py exits non-zero and reports every mismatched row; it never rewrites either value.
quality_gate.behavior_on_missing_tenant_or_date: reported as status=MISSING_IN_SERVING or MISSING_IN_DBT, not silently skipped and not counted as a pass or a numeric mismatch.
